design.name: Data Insight Solutions business card
design.size: 3.5 x 2 in (1050 x 600 px at 300 dpi), two sides

brand.logo: the node-graph mark of this website (assets/DIS-mark.svg)

design.publicCopy: The front is shown as printed. The back is shown without the phone number, by the owner's choice (2026-11-12); email, website and the LinkedIn QR code stay.

designVersions.summary: First export of both sides at 300 dpi, after the logo, rule, teal labels, real contact lines and LinkedIn QR code were set.
The owner enlarged the small text and adjusted the layout in Canva, because the first print on cardstock was not legible.
The owner moved the dot on the back; a pixel comparison showed only the top half of the back changed.

printSheetSpec.layout: 2 columns x 5 rows, 10 cards, cards butted with no gutter
printSheetSpec.bleed: 1/8 in in the card's edge colour
printSheetSpec.duplex: the back page is mirrored so it lines up when flipped on the long edge
printSheetSpec.note: a printed note on the front page tells the printer to print at 100 percent and flip on the long edge

printSheets.why: To see the card on cardstock.

printSheets.what: Rebuilt from the new export in about a minute.
printSheets.why: The small text was not legible on the first print.

printSheets.what: Rebuilt again after the dot on the back moved.
printSheets.why: The design changed, so the sheet made from the old one was out of date.

sheetsPrivate: The print sheets are PDFs kept privately; they carry the full contact line. Only their existence and what they were made from are recorded here.
process: The card was generated in Canva from the website's own colours, fonts and the node-graph logo uploaded from the live site; the owner picked one of four candidates.

It was refined through the Canva connector: the template's face photo replaced by the logo, the rule ending in a logo-style node, teal uppercase labels, real contact lines, and a LinkedIn QR code generated locally (navy on near-white, checked to decode) with a LinkedIn label above it.
The owner set the fonts to IBM Plex Mono in Canva, because the connector cannot change fonts.
Both sides were exported at 300 dpi and a print sheet was built from them (v1).
Printed on cardstock, the small text was not legible; the owner enlarged it and adjusted the layout, and sheet v2 was rebuilt from the new export in about a minute.
The owner moved the dot on the back and sheet v3 was rebuilt; a pixel comparison showed only the top half of the back changed.
The public copy omits the phone number, by the owner's choice.
